seoDescription: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episode 3 review. Chewbacca in handcuffs orc trick, Celeborn in an orc basement, and a humbled Dark Wizard.
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (Season 3, Episode 3)
series: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
excerpt: A predictable fake-out with our leashed orc, topped off by daytime soap opera reunions and a Dark Wizard getting bullied in Rhûn.
body: Episode three rolled around and I found myself nodding off again, only to wake up right as our friendly neighbourhood "Good Orc" Marnûkh was delivering Guyladriel and Arondir straight to the gates of Mount Gundabad. The show tries to play this like a sudden betrayal, like oh no, did the orc trick them after all? Please. If you have watched a single action movie in the last forty years, you know the Chewbacca in handcuffs trick. He is marching them in as fake prisoners so they can infiltrate the tower and reach the elven smith. It is not a twist, it is just lazy plotting pretending to be clever.

The real joke is what happens once they actually get inside. All that trekking through the dirt with an orc on a leash to find Celebrimbor's secret ring apprentice, and she has been dead for weeks. Total waste of time. But Amazon cannot help itself, so instead of the smith, who do they find sitting in the very next cell? Celeborn. Yes, Galadriel's long-lost husband, who has been missing since season one and presumed dead, was apparently just chilling in an orc basement this whole time. It is straight out of a daytime soap opera. The writing is so contrived you can practically hear the writers room high-fiving each other over finding an excuse to finally bring him back.

Over in Rhûn, we get the other major thread of the week, and it does not fare much better. The Dark Wizard, played by Ciarán Hinds, is sitting around whining about a withered flower and hoping to get his hands on a ring to fix his landscaping. Instead, Sauron sends Khamûl the Easterling to deliver a reality check. Khamûl is already rocking his ring and Nazgûl powers, and he completely dogs the Dark Wizard. He snaps the stone in his staff and forces this ancient, supposedly terrifying sorcerer to take a knee and pledge allegiance to Mordor.

And what are Gandalf and Tom Bombadil doing during this massive power shift? Absolutely nothing. They are crouched on a ridge like spectators at a tennis match, whispering exposition and watching Sauron lock down Rhûn without lifting a finger to stop it.

That leaves us with Númenor, which has now decamped to the Western Havens so Elendil and his son Anárion can mope around planning a rebellion against Ar-Pharazôn. The momentum here is practically non-existent. Every time an episode feels like it might actually kick into high gear, the show cuts to another location for fifteen minutes of stiff dialogue and political wheel-spinning. The visual effects are still carrying this entire billion dollar production on their back, but beneath the shiny gloss, the narrative engine is running completely empty. Another easy 3/10.
verdict: 3/10: A predictable fake-out with our leashed orc, topped off by daytime soap opera reunions and a Dark Wizard getting bullied in Rhûn.
